feasibility.rule_applied: Every suggestion must still cover the daily route plus a 20 % reserve when the pack is due for replacement.
feasibility.plain: Today, when this pack has aged to the replacement line it can still drive about 210 km on a charge. Your route needs 180 km (150 km plus a 20 % reserve), so there is room to spare.

not_used.reason: Halving or doubling charger power moves battery life by at most 1.5 months in the model. In the NREL models charge speed has almost no effect on cycling loss within the tested range, so power only changes how long the pack sits full. Not worth changing for battery health.

effect_months.note: largest change in median life when charger power is halved or doubled

not_used.reason: Both NREL cells were cycled at 80 to 100 % depth of discharge. A bus uses less than that, so the model is extrapolating, and any gain from changing the minimum charge cannot be trusted. It is also a safety margin rather than a battery-usage choice, so it is never suggested.
Daily distance is a service level set by the operator, not a battery-usage choice, so it is not changed. You can still explore it by editing Bus B by hand.

notes: Presets are suggestions to test, not predictions that they will be followed.
Cost per km moves in step with battery life here because the pack price and daily distance are held fixed.
18 combinations of charge cap and start time passed the route rule; 4 charge caps failed it.
warnings: Prior mode: capacity curves come from published laboratory-fitted LFP cell models (NREL BLAST-Lite) and scenario inputs are assumptions. Nothing here has been validated on buses.
Depth-of-discharge effects on cycle fade are not modelled (training cycles were full-depth).
Cell temperature = air temperature + an assumed constant heat rise; no thermal-management data exists for buses.
